title: Transmission Electron Microscopy Protocol for Observing Secretory Spines
author: Mario Alberto Sandoval-Molina
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k3xcypn

steps.title: Prepare Medium Hardness Spurr's Resin
steps.instruction: Prepare approximately 21 g of resin by mixing the following components, adding the accelerator last and keeping the mixture at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Combine 5.0 g V.C.D., 3.0 g D.E.R., and 13.0 g N.S.A.
Stir the mixture during preparation.
Add 0.4 g D.M.A.E. (accelerator) last.

steps.title: Embed Tissues in Resin
steps.instruction: Infiltrate dehydrated tissues (100% ethanol) with Spurr's resin at 4 °C through a series of concentrations for 2 hours each.

substeps.instruction: Transfer tissues to 3:1 (ethanol: Spurr's resin).
Transfer tissues to 1:1 (ethanol: Spurr's resin).
Transfer tissues to 1:3 (ethanol: Spurr's resin).
Transfer tissues to 100% Spurr's resin.

steps.title: Orient and Polymerize Samples
steps.instruction: Orient secretory spines for longitudinal sections in flat embedding moulds and polymerize at 60 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Cut and Stain Semi-Thin Sections
steps.instruction: Obtain semi-thin longitudinal and transverse sections (1-2 µm) using an ultra-microtome (Ultracut, Reichert-Jung) and glass knives, then stain with 1% toluidine blue.

substeps.instruction: Prepare staining solution: Dissolve 2 g Sodium Borate (Borax) in 100 mL distilled water, then add 1 g Toluidine Blue powder and stir until dissolved.
Collect sections on a glass slide and dry on a slide warmer at 60 °C.
Cover dried sections with a few drops of staining solution (while heat source is still on) for 1-2 minutes.
Gently rinse off excess stain with distilled water.
Air dry the slide and coverslip with oil immersion medium.

steps.title: Prepare Ultrathin Sections
steps.instruction: Obtain ultrathin (80 nm) sections using an ultra-microtome (Ultracut, Reichert-Jung) with a 6 mm glass knife.

substeps.instruction: Collect sections on 200 mesh copper grids coated with formvar/carbon (Agar Scientific).

steps.title: Perform Double Staining
steps.instruction: Apply a double staining procedure using uranyl acetate and lead citrate.

substeps.instruction: Immerse sections in 2% uranyl acetate in 70% ethanol for 40 min.
Rinse three times for 30 min each in double distilled water.
Stain with Lead Citrate solution for 2 min.
Wash three times for 2 min each and rinse three times for 10 min each in double distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare Lead Citrate Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh lead citrate solution according to the Reynolds (1963) method.

substeps.instruction: Boil distilled water for 10 min to obtain CO2-free distilled water.
In a 50 mL volumetric flask, combine 1.33 g lead nitrate [Pb(NO3)2], 1.76 g sodium citrate [Na(C6H5O7)2H2O], and 30 mL CO2-free distilled water.
Shake the mixture at intervals for about 30 min until a milky suspension forms.
Add 8 mL of 1 N NaOH (prepared with CO2-free distilled water).
Bring the total volume to 50 mL with CO2-free distilled water and mix by inversion until the solution clears and lead citrate dissolves completely.

steps.title: Perform TEM Observations
steps.instruction: Observe samples using a TEM microscope (JEOL JEM 12000 EII) at 80 kV and digitally record images.
